title: Sweetheart Corset Top Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Fitted sleeveless top with a sweetheart neckline and button back

Level Intermediate

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Cotton sateen, cotton poplin, linen, chambray or light denim

Pieces 6

This free sweetheart corset top sewing pattern gives you a fitted, sleeveless top with a softly pointed sweetheart neckline, wide straps and a row of eleven small buttons down the back. Bust and waist darts shape it like a corset, with no boning and no lace-up, so it stays easy to sew and comfortable to wear.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the front and back · 11 buttons, 1 cm (3/8″)

Design details of the sweetheart corset top

The look is corset-inspired but the sewing is classic dressmaking. A side bust dart and a long waist dart on each side of the front, plus a shoulder dart and a waist dart on each back panel, give the close, sculpted shape, with about 5.5 cm of ease at the bust. The neckline, the full-length back opening and the armholes are all finished with interfaced facings, so nothing shows on the outside.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the two straight lines from the shoulders turn into two soft curves that meet in a point: that is the sweetheart neckline. The short horizontal lines at the sides are the bust darts, and the two long vertical lines from below the bust to the hem are the waist darts. There are no seams in the middle and no buttons on the front.

On the back you can see the opening at the centre back with its eleven buttons, a short dart from each shoulder and a long waist dart on each side. The back neckline sits high and is gently curved.

  • Sweetheart neckline with a pointed centre front, finished with an interfaced facing
  • Wide straps about 9.5 cm (3 3/4″) and clean faced armholes
  • Side bust darts and front waist darts, shoulder and waist darts at the back
  • Full-length back opening with 11 buttons, 1 cm (3/8″)
  • High-hip length with a straight hem, 2 cm (3/4″) hem allowance

It is a lovely project once you have made a few easy tops: no sleeves and no zipper, but you will practise darts, a pointed facing and a neat row of buttonholes on a top that looks like it came from a boutique.

Sizing guide

Measure your bust around the fullest part and pick the size from the table, then check your waist and hips. This top is fitted: between two sizes, choose by the bust and adjust the waist at the side seams. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished top measurements

There is about 5.5 cm (2 1/8″) of ease at the bust and 7 cm (2 3/4″) at the waist. Back length is measured at the centre back from the neckline seam to the finished hem; front length from the shoulder at the neck to the hem.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out for each size, plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. Buy a little more for a one-way print, stripes or checks, and pre-wash the fabric before cutting.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The top is drafted for 167.75 cm and ends at the high hip. Change the hem of the front and back by the same amount, change the lower end of the back neck facing to match and re-space the lowest buttons. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Neckline depth. The point of the sweetheart sits about 22 cm (8 5/8″) below the shoulder in size 8. To raise it, trace the front and the front neck facing and move the point up by the same amount on both, keeping the curves smooth.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 0.9 to 1.4 m (1 to 1 5/8 yd) of a light to medium-weight woven with a little body
  • Interfacing: 0.7 m (7/8 yd) of light to medium fusible interfacing for the facings
  • Buttons: 11 buttons, 1 cm (3/8″), the same for all sizes
  • Thread: polyester all-purpose thread
  • Tools: buttonhole foot, universal needle 70 to 80, a tailor's ham for pressing the darts
  • Pins or clips, chalk or a washable marker

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1 on a single layer, right side up (drawn whole)
  • 2 Back: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 3 Front neck facing: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing (drawn whole)
  • 4 Front armhole facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing
  • 5 Back neck facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing (runs down the whole back opening)
  • 6 Back armhole facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing

Choosing fabric for a sweetheart corset top

A fitted top with darts needs a fabric that holds its shape. Cotton sateen gives the polished, slightly shiny corset look; cotton poplin, linen, chambray and light denim are perfect for everyday versions, and a jacquard or brocade turns it into an evening top. The point of the sweetheart neckline stays crisp in all of them.

Because the top is close fitting, a woven with 2 to 3 % elastane is comfortable without changing the size. Avoid knits and very soft, slippery fabrics such as satin or chiffon: the darts and the buttonholes will be hard to keep neat. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to use fusible interfacing.

  1. How to take your body measurements: what to measure and how, in 10 minutes.
  2. How to choose your size: which measurement to follow, and what to do between sizes.
  3. How to print and assemble your pattern: A4 or US Letter, the test box, and taping the pages. Then learn how to read a sewing pattern: symbols and markings explained.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A close, corset-like fit from bust to high hip. Pin the darts and try the front on before you sew the facings if you are between sizes.

Fabric

Wovens with body only. Press every dart over a tailor's ham and use a pressing cloth on sateen to avoid shine.

Buttons

Eleven horizontal buttonholes on the right back. See how to sew buttonholes and buttons.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together and press every seam and dart before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse interfacing to all the facings. Transfer the darts, notches, the centre back line and the button marks. Staystitch the front neckline 8 mm from the edge, from each shoulder towards the point, with a shorter stitch near the point, and staystitch the back necklines.
  2. Front darts. Sew the bust darts from the side seam towards the point, then the waist darts from the upper point down to the hem edge. Knot the thread tails at the points, press the bust darts down and the waist darts towards the centre.
  3. Back darts. Sew the shoulder darts from the shoulder towards the point and the waist darts from the upper point to the hem. Press them towards the centre back.
  4. Shoulders. Pin the front to the backs at the shoulders, stitch, finish the edges separately and press the seams open.
  5. Neckline and back opening. Join the front neck facing to the two back neck facings at the shoulders and finish the outer edge. Pin the facing to the garment along both back opening edges and around the whole neckline, with the centre front notch on the sweetheart point. Stitch in one seam from the hemline on one back edge, up, around the neckline (pivot exactly on the point) and down the other back edge. Trim, clip the curves and clip right into the point, understitch, turn and press.
  6. Side seams. Pin the front to the back at the sides, matching the waist notches, and stitch from the armhole to the hem. Finish and press open.
  7. Armhole facings. Join each front armhole facing (single notch) to a back armhole facing (double notch) at the shoulder and the side to make a ring. Sew it to the armhole, trim and clip, understitch, turn inside and tack at the seams.
  8. Hem. Finish the lower edge and turn up 2 cm (3/4″). Stitch by machine or with a blind hem between the back facings, then fold the lower end of each facing under by 1 cm and slipstitch it over the hem.
  9. Buttons. Lap the right back over the left. Make 11 horizontal buttonholes, 1.2 cm long, on the right back at the marks, starting 3 mm past the centre back line, and sew the buttons on the left back. Give the top a final press.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the darts and the sweetheart facing to the buttonholes
  • Size charts in cm and inches, finished measurements and fabric amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes
  • Printable PDF with A0 pattern files, instant download
Shop now

Tips and common mistakes

A sweetheart point that puckers. Shorten the stitch near the point, stop with the needle down exactly on it before you pivot, and clip into the point right up to the stitching. Understitch as far into the point as you can.

Dart tips that bubble. Sew the last 2 cm of each dart right along the fold, do not backstitch at the tip, knot the threads instead and press over a tailor's ham.

A back opening that gapes. Interface the whole back facing and space the buttonholes exactly on the marks; check the fit before you cut the buttonholes open.

Facings that roll out. Grade the seam allowances, understitch every facing and tack it to the shoulder and side seam allowances by hand.

How to style a sweetheart corset top

Everyday: with light-wash straight jeans and flat sandals, or over a white tee for a layered look.

Polished: tuck-free over high-waisted wide-leg trousers. It pairs beautifully with our free wide leg pants sewing pattern.

Evening: in black jacquard or cherry red sateen with a satin skirt and small gold earrings. For a matching outfit, try our free flare pants sewing pattern.

Care

Wash at 30 °C on a gentle cycle, inside out, with the buttons closed. Dry on a hanger and press from the wrong side; use a pressing cloth on sateen and a little steam on the darts.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every edge, plus a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the front and back.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust measurement in the size chart, not by your shop size. The top is fitted, with about 5.5 cm (2 1/8″) of ease at the bust: between two sizes, choose by the bust and adjust the waist at the side seams.

Is this a real corset?

No. It is a corset-style top: the close shape comes from bust darts and waist darts, with no boning, no lace-up and no busk, so it is comfortable to wear all day and easy to sew on a home machine.

How do I get it on?

The back opens from the neckline to the hem and closes with 11 small buttons, so the fitted top goes on like a waistcoat worn back to front.

Is this sweetheart top hard to sew?

It is a good intermediate project. There are six pieces and no sleeves, but you will sew darts, a pointed neckline with a facing, armhole facings and 11 buttonholes.

What fabric works best?

A light to medium-weight woven with a little body: cotton sateen, cotton poplin, linen, chambray, light denim or a jacquard for evening. A woven with 2 to 3 % elastane is comfortable and needs no size change.

Can I make it longer or shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Change the hem of the front and back by the same amount, shorten or lengthen the lower end of the back neck facing to match, and re-space the lowest buttons.
